correctness.rationale: For 3|m, the average squared vertex radius bound forces center zero and circumradius<=1 with equality only vertex triples. Otherwise dihedral symmetry reduces orientation to [0,pi/(3m)]; weighted polygon supporting normals eliminate the free center and yield a strict orientation certificate (B>A tan(delta/2)). A constructed triangle centered at (1-R,0) makes all normal constraints nonpositive and saturates the bound. Equality constraints force unique center for canonical orientation and the m-orbit classification. Independent 3-variable linear programming enumerated 6 orientations each for m=3..20 and matched the sharp formula, including noncanonical strict gaps.
